subject: Mathematics

definitions.definition: An equation in which the highest power of the variable is 1. It is of the form ax + b = c, where a ≠ 0.
The value of the variable that satisfies the equation (makes both sides equal).
Moving a term from one side of the equation to another, changing its sign.

formulae.name: General Linear Equation
formulae.formula: ax + b = c → x = (c - b) / a
formulae.used_for: Finding the value of unknown variable

important_concepts: A linear equation has exactly one solution
Both sides of an equation can be multiplied or divided by the same non-zero number
The same number can be added or subtracted from both sides
Word problems: identify the unknown, form equation, solve
Equations with variables on both sides: bring all variables to one side
common_mistakes: Changing sign incorrectly when transposing terms
Not performing the same operation on both sides
Error in setting up equations from word problems
Dividing by zero when coefficient becomes zero
